known_facts_book1: The lovely Ruler of the Land of Oz, who never leaves the Emerald City in this book and acts entirely through her Magic Picture and the Wizard's magic.
Watches the whole adventure day by day in a Magic Picture in a radium frame in her boudoir, with the Wizard seated beside her.
Sent Tik-Tok to tell Shaggy where his brother was, having seen both in the Magic Picture, and let Shaggy take the Love Magnet from the gateway of the Emerald City.
Is entirely unaware of the Army of Oogaboo's plan to conquer her; Glinda deals with it without ever mentioning it to her.
Has the Wizard send Ann, her officers, Files and the Rose Princess home to Oogaboo, keeping Files and Ozga together because they have become such good friends.
Speaks with Shaggy by a wireless telephone of the Wizard's invention, two tiny instruments held to the ear that need no wire.
Holds that the Land of Oz is not a refuge for all mortals in distress and that Shaggy's brother has no claim on her — and admits him anyway rather than lose Shaggy.
Gives Betsy a suite of rooms opposite Dorothy's and orders a golden stall built for Hank beside the Sawhorse.
Rebukes the Sawhorse, the Lion and the Tiger for quarreling, saying Oz is a Land of Love where friendship outranks every other quality.
Reveals that the spell of the fairyland has given Toto speech too, and that he simply prefers not to talk.

known_facts_book1: A Princess of Oz living in Ozma's palace, who came to the Land of Oz from the United States and is known to Shaggy as an old chum.
Does not appear until the last two chapters; before that she is only spoken of by others.
Has watched Betsy and Hank in the Magic Picture and already thinks Betsy a dear little girl and Hank a darling.
Is asked by Ozma for advice on admitting the strangers, and answers that they cannot afford to lose their Shaggy Man.
Runs down the stairs two at a time to meet Betsy herself, so the new girl will not feel strange in the big palace.
Owns a Pink Kitten upstairs in her room that talks very nicely, and Toto, who has been with her in Oz a long time and has never said a word.
Blows a small silver whistle to call Toto, and coaxes one sentence out of him: 'All right. Here I go!'
Is defended in the stable by the Cowardly Lion, the Hungry Tiger and the Sawhorse as the dearest, sweetest girl in the world.

known_facts_book1: The little Wizard of Oz, who came to the Land of Oz from the United States and sits beside Ozma watching the Magic Picture.
Invented the wireless telephone — two tiny instruments held to the ear that record the same vibrations and need no wire connection.
Transports the Oogaboo party home and later Shaggy, his brother, Betsy and Hank into Oz, using a silver plate, a pink powder from a crystal vial, and an incantation Glinda the Good taught him.
The transportation ends in a puff of pungent perfumed smoke, which he says is a very necessary part of his wizardry.
Is described in this book only as Ozma's attendant and magician; he never leaves the palace and never meets Ruggedo.

known_facts_book1: Dorothy's little fuzzy black dog, who has been with her in Oz a long time and has never said anything but 'Bow-wow!'
Appears only in the final chapter, running up the path when Dorothy blows her silver whistle.
Is revealed by Ozma to have been under the fairyland's speech spell all along — he understands everything and simply prefers not to talk.
Answers Dorothy with his bark and his tail, 'Bow-wow' meaning yes and 'Woof' meaning no.
Finally says one sentence — 'All right. Here I go!' — and darts away as swift as an arrow.

known_facts_book1: Ozma's favorite steed, a wooden horse with knot eyes and a branch for a tail, living in a gold-panelled stall in the stable behind the palace.
Is shod with plates of gold and never sleeps, so he has no need of the cushions Hank is given.
Is the only horse of any description in the Land of Oz.
Questions Hank about whether 'hee-haw' is all he can say, and tells him all animals talk in Oz.
Declares that no girl living can compare with his mistress Ozma, and snorts and stamps when Hank claims Betsy is the sweetest girl in the world.
Shakes hoofs with Hank after Ozma's rebuke.

known_facts_book1: One of Ozma's beasts, living in the stable behind the palace in a room filled with soft cushions and a golden trough.

Declares he will fight anyone, animal or human, who denies that Dorothy is the dearest, sweetest girl in the world, because she was his first friend and companion.
Tells Hank that any friend of a friend of their beloved Ruler is a friend of the Cowardly Lion, and offers him help or advice whenever he needs it.
Says there are other Lions in Oz besides himself.
